title: A pre-1997 linear regional transfer left a 2010-2021 runoff deficit in mainland south-east Australia
abstract: We tested whether simultaneous runoff anomalies outside mainland south-east Australia could account for its later deficit. Local weather models and regional transfer fits used years before 1997. Northern Australia, south-west Western Australia and Tasmania supplied donor indices. Earlier forward tests selected the ridge penalty. The primary 2010-2021 departure was -20.33% of reference mean runoff. Regional transfer predicted -2.57% and left -17.76% (conditional 95% limits -34.28 to -5.27). The later error gain was uncertain. Common year blocks and spatial cells supplied the limits, conditional on local weather curves and model selection. The result limits this stable linear regional transfer. It does not exclude local or changing climatic effects, or establish a physical cause. This secondary analysis reuses CAMELS-AUS annual tables from a verified SCI publication. The primary transfer did not improve earlier validation. A simpler weather variant improved validation by 16.83% but still left a -17.40% later departure (-31.88 to -4.64).

display.caption: Observed regional residuals, predictions from three donor regions, and remaining 2010-2021 departures. Limits resample shared year blocks and spatial cells, conditional on the local weather models.
